name: Bitter bamboo
summary: Forest bamboo with a sweet-bitter taste. The culture desk lists it stir-fried with fermented rice, boiled, grilled, stewed with bone, or made into a salad. Vietnamnet adds a dip of chẩm chéo and says the bitterness is the point. A season and a price are Check on arrival.
origin: Dien Bien Phu. The culture desk does not pin a ward. Vietnamnet calls it a common plate and does not name a street.
taste: The culture desk says the sweet-bitter taste of forest bamboo stays however it is cooked. Vietnamnet says grilled shoots keep the bitter and the astringent, and that this bamboo is not soaked in salt to strip the bitterness the way other fresh bamboo is.
howToEat: The culture desk: stir-fry with fermented rice, boil, grill, stew with bone, or make a salad.
Vietnamnet’s simplest plate is boiled bamboo with chẩm chéo. It also names stir-fry, boiling, grilling, and a bone stew.
A single house style, a season, and a price are Check on arrival.
where: The provincial table. Neither account names a ward or a shop. A stall hour is Check on arrival.
